**OFFENSIVE TERMINOLOGY** 

**PERSONNEL GROUPS** 

**(R) REGULAR (21) 2 RB, 1 TE, 2 WR** 

**(T) TIGER (12) 1 RB, 2 TE, 2 WR (2ND TE BECOMES THE ‘F’) (CB) CUB (12) (2ND TE BECOMES THE ‘Y’)** 

**(U) U (22) 2 RB, 2 TE, 1 WR (2ND TE BECOMES THE ‘U’) (Y) Y (22) (‘U’ Replaces ‘X’)  (‘2ND TE BECOMES THE ‘Y’)** 

**(ZE) ZEBRA (11) 1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR (3RD WR BECOMES THE ‘F’)** 

**(TR) TREY (13) 1 RB, 3 TE, 1 WR (2 TE’s BECOME THE ‘U’ & ‘F’ U’ Replaces ‘X’)** 

**(TRY) TREY-Y (13) 1 RB, 3 TE, 1 WR THE ‘Y’ ‘BECOMES THE ’ U ‘ (CLB) CLUBS (13H) 1 RB, 2 TE, 1 WR (‘1’ Extra O Lineman)** 

**(B) BEAST (22H) 2 RB, 1 TE, 1 WR (‘1’ Extra O Lineman) (KD) KODIAK (12H) 1 RB, 1 TE, 2 WR (‘1’ Extra O Lineman)** 

**(MUS) MUSCLE (23) 2 RB, 3 TE, 0 WR (2 TE’s BECOME THE ‘U’ & ‘Z’) (‘U’ Replaces ‘X’)** 

**(MON) MONSTER (23HH) 2 RB, 1 TE, 0 WR (‘2’ Extra O Lineman) (ZEUS) ZEUS (23H) 2 RB, 2 TE, 0 WR (‘1’ Extra O Lineman)** 

**PERSONNEL VARIATIONS** 

**(ZCH) CHEETAH (02) 0 RB, 2 TE, 3 WR (3RD WR BECOMES THE ‘F’) (2ND Replaces ‘H’)** 

**(P) PANTHER (01) 0 RB, 1 TE, 4 WR (4TH WR BECOMES THE ‘H’) (EA) EAGLE (10) 1 RB, 0 TE, 4 WR (3RD & 4TH WRs BECOME THE ‘F’ & ‘Y’) (UH) UHUSKER (31) 3 RB, 1 TE, 1 WR (‘3rd’ RB BECOMES THE ‘Z’) (E) E (20) 2 RB, 0 TE, 3 WR (3RD WR BECOMES THE ‘Y’) (PNY) PONY (21) 2 HB, 1 TE, 2 WR (2ND HB BECOMES THE ‘F’) (ST) STAR 0 RB, 0 TE, 5 WR (5TH WR BECOMES THE ‘H’) (ARB) ARABIAN 3 HB, 0 TE, 2 WR (3RD HB BECOMES THE ‘Y’) (ACE) ACE (14HH) 1 RB, 2 TE, 0 WR (‘2’ Extra O Lineman)**  
**HUDDLE MECHANICS**   
**FORMING AND BREAKING THE HUDDLE** 1\) Center always sets up huddle 7 yards from the ball. Set up quickly. 2\) Center calls “Huddle Up”. The personnel will align on the center quickly and efficiently. 3\) Huddle is oval with the Offensive Line closest to the ball – hands on knees and eyes up. **REGULAR GROUPING**   
7 YDSBALL   
C Q Z **F** Y   
RG LT RT LG   
X   
HB   
**4\) Quarterback has complete control of the huddle** 5\) You will receive the following information in the huddle a. Formation (Shift / Motion possible) b. Play c. Blocking d. Pass Pattern (possible) e. Snap Count **Twice** 6\) When you do not hear what is said, call “**Check**” 7\) “**Ready-Break**” is the signal to leave the huddle a. Clap hands and say “BREAK” 8\) WR’s leave after they have heard the first snap count called a. WR’s sprint out of the huddle to get aligned and set (especially if any kind of motion /shift is on) b. The rest of the Offensive Line will hustle to the L.O.S. after the snap count is repeated the second time, **TEMPO** is key\! 9\) Well disciplined huddle and break is a reflection of our offense and how we operate. Keep it sharp and take pride in it\! **U GROUPING**

HUDDLE PROCEDURES   
IN THE HUDDLE We have 40/25 seconds to snap the next play. It is important that we are efficient with our huddle mechanics to give ourselves adequate time at the L.O.S. The Left tackle will call out the Down and Distance. Personnel entering the huddle will echo the personnel group as they approach the huddle. ONCE QB ENTERS HUDDLE, QB DOES ALL THE TALKING. HE WILL GIVE THE FOLLOWING INFORMATION: 1\) Shift (Scatter to, Y Shift to) 2\) Formation (Green, Red, Double, Trips, etc) 3\) Formation Direction (Right or Left) 4\) Formation Variation (Slot, Nasty , etc) 5\) Motion (F-Short, F- Counter, H- Right O, etc) 6\) Play Number (96, Nickel 40, 2 JET, etc) 7\) Play Terms (Power, “Y” Stick, “Z Cujo”) 8\) Snap Count (pause) (WR’s leave early) Snap Count (On Set, On Ducks, On One, On Two) 9\) “Ready-Break” HERE’S HOW IT SOUNDS 1\) Y Shift to Dot Rt, 96 Zone Kill 97 Zone, On One, On One, Ready-Break 2\) Green Rt Slot ‘Z’ Rt. 96 Boss, On Two, On Two, Ready-Break 3\) Green Rt Fox 2 Double Go, On Sunday, On Sunday, Ready-Break 4\) Double Rt Z-Short 2 Jet Z-Drive X Crush, On Ducks, On Ducks, Ready-Break  
**10 ![][image3]***Confidential Property of the San Francisco 49ers*   
**AT THE LINE OF SCRIMMAGE (L.O.S.)** 1\) O-Line and TE get up and get in your appropriate stance. Center will call out the front. 2\) QB calls the “Set-Hut”, then Color and Number to each side (Color-\#) 3\) QB pauses and completes the snap count as follows: “Hut” (if on one) 4\) The snap count is non-rhythmic through the 1stcolor-number, pause. The QB should vary this part of the count accordingly. The 2nd color-number is rhythmic and rolls into the first “Hut”. 5\) When QB calls the snap count on Two (2nd hut), he will try to draw the defense offsides on the 1stHut by accentuating the count – pause – and then “Hut.” **Everyone must have great poise** – do not jump\! 6\) If a Defender jumps in the neutral zone on the first hut, the OL across from him should respond quickly with a “flash” technique; Quick set to draw a defensive penalty and stoppage of play. *Note: We want to mix up our snap counts when possible to make the defense react to us\! This involves plays with motions so the defense cannot time up their get-off\! **SNAP COUNTS:*** 1\) **Sunday, Sunday** \- “**SET HUT\!”** 2\) On **Ducks** \- **“SET HUT-HUT\!”** 3\) On **One \- “SET HUT, Color-\#, Color-\#, HUT\!”** 4\) On **Two \- “SET HUT, Color-\#, Color-\#, HUT-HUT\!” DOUBLE/TRIPLE COUNTS**: A ‘Double Count’(D.C.) is a dummy-cadence used to assess the defense as well as mix up our tempo on the defense at the LOS. The prescribed ‘Double Count’ is used by the QB, followed by an on One snap count that begins at the 1stcolor-number. 1\) On **“Double Count \- Ducks”** “Set \- HUT \- HUT… Red-80, Red-80 \- HUT\!” 2\) On **“Double Count \- One”**   
“Set HUT \- Red-80, Red-80 \- HUT\!”...Red-80, Red-80 \- HUT\!” **EXPRESS** If we are running out of time on the play clock, and are in danger of a delay of game penalty, the QB is responsible to adjust with EXPRESS mechanics. EXPRESS mechanics call for the entire offense to line up in the final formation, snap the ball on “DUCKS”, and execute the play called. Any shift or motion is cancelled. Once the QB communicates EXPRESS, everyone on the offense must understand we are short on time and we must react quickly and efficiently. EXPRESS mechanics call for the ball to be snapped on **DUCKS***Confidential Property of the San Francisco 49ers* **11 ![][image4]**  
**“FREDDY”** 

Freddy is a method to align on the ball and call the best offensive play based on the deployment of the defense. 

1\) The QB will set us into Freddy mechanics by calling out:  

A. “FREDDY, FREDDY” 

2\) The QB will call out a formation:  

A. “DEUCE RT, DEUCE RT” 

B. The offense will align in this formation in good stances. 

3\) The QB will call out ***“Dummy Verbiage,”*** followed by ***“Dummy Ducks***” snap count. A. Example: “Florida Gators 86, Florida Gators 86, Roger, Roger” 

B. “Set, Hut, Hut” 

4\) Once the QB finishes his dummy-ducks count, the next call is the live play followed by a live Ducks  snap count. 

A. “Lions-Punch...Lions-Punch…Set, Hut, Hut” 

5\) We will execute 94 Punch on Ducks. 

**FREDDY COMMUNICATION AT THE LOS** 

1\. FORMATION 

2\. DUMMY VERBIAGE 

3\. DUMMY DUCKS COUNT 

4\. CODED PLAY CALL 

5\. DUCKS SNAP COUNT (LIVE) 

**NASCAR** 

Nascar is used to hurry to the line of scrimmage and have the QB call out a formation and play that we  execute on a DUCKS Snap Count. There is no dummy verbiage. 

**NASCAR COMMUNICATION AT THE LOS** 

1\. FORMATION 

2\. PLAY CALL 

3\. DUCKS SNAP COUNT 

\---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- **INSTANT** 

When we want to run a play as quickly as possible with no personnel substitution, we will call  “INSTANT”. No matter the personnel, we will align in **DOUBLE RT** and execute **94 PUNCH** On **SUNDAY.** We want to execute this quickly and efficiently, everyone get set\!

**FORMATIONS** The ability to use multiple formations, substitutions and motions allows us to manipulate our opponent’s defense to our advantage. The key to this type of flexibility is to fully understand our formation system. In order to do this each player must understand our base formations, then be able to apply the multiple variations to them.**SPLIT ALIGNMENTS** 1\. MINUS 2 (-2 YARDS FROM INSIDE EDGE OF \#s) 2\. **MOTIONS** 1\. Motions are used to get a reaction out of a defense or create an advantage for the offense. All motions are fast, crisp and will be executed with a sense of urgency. 2\. Techniques of motions: ∙ **Shuffle**: Square up and shuffle at the end of your landmark (2-3 yds prior to snap point). ∙ **Sideline**: Traditional motion keeping your shoulders towards the sideline at your motion landmark. 3\. QB will start by giving a heel and will be in charge of deployment and motion landmarks. Final responsibility falls on the player in motion. In the ‘Gun’, QB will use Hand to start motion. 4\. If two (2) men are mistakenly in motion, the QB should ‘**FREEZE**’ everyone for 1 second, and everyone should line up in the final formation called, making the play legal\!

**SHIFTS** We use shifts to help identify coverages and to make the defense have to think and communicate more. Let’s take pride in our shifts. Make sure we communicate on and off with hand gestures so there are no mental breakdowns...let’s make it “Easy for us and Hard for Them”\! When a shift is called in the huddle, we quickly get to the L.O.S. to show the defense a pre-snap formation. It must be a believable formation to the defense. Great stances\! Important Notes on Legally Shifting: A. “Non-Abrupt” movement of the head and/or shoulders is legal. B. Players must come to a Stop for 1 full second before the ball is snapped. As a general rule, the QB should show the beginning formation for 1 full second to get the defense to honor the formation. C. No offensive player should “simulate the start of a play”. D. All Ineligible offensive Linemen: Once you take “or simulate” a 3-point stance, you cannot lift your hand up\! There are Three (3) Shift Mechanics we will use: 1\. Call a shift that tells the offense to line up in a formation and shift to the final formation called on the “MOVE” command by the QB. These can be: 1\. ‘**Named Shifts**’ (Shift is given a codeword) ex: ‘**Blast**’ to Double Right 2\. ‘**Shift to**’ (beginning formation called, then final formation called) ex: Weak Rt ‘**Shift to**’ Tin Bunch Rt 2\. Call a ‘Reset’ motion to a formation on double count, then call a shift to a final formation on the QB “MOVE” command. Players not involved in the shift need to line up in the final formation called. ex: **‘F’ Reset** to: Deuce Rt, ‘**Shift to**’ Trips Lt ex: **‘Z’ Reset** to: Green Rt, ‘**Shift to**’ Tin Bunch Rt 3\. ‘**DOCKERS**’ calls for the offense to Line up in a called formation, use Double Count mechanics and Shift to a final formation on the ‘HUT’ of the double count. It is important not to use sudden movements when shifting on the QB ‘HUT’. ex: Green Rt, ‘**Dockers Y-Shift**’ to Green Lt ex: Dot Rt, ‘**Dockers Shift**’ to Tin Bunch Rt ex: ‘**Dockers Lava**’ to Weak Rt Heavy Wing

**“SALOON” SHIFTS** The term “Saloon” before a playcall lets both tackles know we may shift them as part of our advantage system. This alerts them to **start in a two-point stance** until the QB confirms the play we will run at the LOS. Specific Words will key pre-snap shift rules, formation rules and play. Ex: “**Ranger-9**”- **Rope-Shift to a Heavy Bunch Lt and execute 99 Truck**. RT Shift sides. Truck Pull. LT slide to Loose split. Execute crack block. Outside Receiver to \# – Adjust split to 2 yds. from OT / ON LOS. Execute Seal Block. F – Shift to Tin Lt Location. Execute Pull and Kickout. “**Laredo-8**” \- **Lava-Shift to a Heavy Bunch Lt and execute 99 Truck**. LT Shift sides to Loose split. Execute crack block. Outside Receiver to \# – Adjust split to 2 yds. from OT / ON LOS. Execute Seal Block. F – Shift to Tin Rt Location. Execute Pull and Kickout.

**HEAVY SHIFTS** When we shift an Offensive Lineman, it is important that any Lineman involved in the shift does NOT put his hand down before the Shift. We will be specific in how we call these ‘heavy’ shifts. WR’s must be keyed in to being ON or OFF the ball before and after a shift\! As a general rule...don’t cover up a TE and make sure to cover up a Lineman\! When shifting behind the QB, the OL will have the right of way and the TE will go behind him. We will shift on the “Move” command by the QB. **HEAVY SHIFTS**

**DEFENSIVE COVERAGES** 

Defensive Coverage Concepts are defined by Numbers. **COVERAGE NUMBERING** 

Cover 0 \- Man Across.  

Cover 1 \- Man Free. 

Cover 2 \- Two Deep  

Cover 3 \- Three-deep Zone. 

Cover 4/6 — Four-deep Zone/Cloud Wk. or Str. 

Cover 5 \- Double or Bracket Man. 

Variations of each coverage are described with words. **COVERAGE TAGS** 

‘sky’ \- Strong Safety as a Force/Flat defender 

‘cloud’ \- Corner as a Force/Flat defender 

‘press’ \- Indicates Corner in tight alignment to WR 

‘dog’ \- Indicates LB Rush, 5 or more  

‘blitz’ \- Indicates Secondary Rush, 5 or more 

‘match’ \- Zone Coverage with Man Inside  

‘man’ \- Man Under Coverage  

‘robber’ \- Strong Safety Invert as Hole player 

‘lurk’ \- Free Safety Invert as Hole player 

‘buzz’ \- Safety invert as Hook-Curl player 

‘tampa’ \- MLB running deep middle 

‘clue’ \- Corner/Safety reading 2-1 vs Slot Look 

‘invert’ \- Safety and Corner Exchange responsibilities ‘cut’ \- Cloud Coverage behind a SS Blitz 

‘palms’ \- A clue 4-Across/2-Under Pressure Coverage
